decisions.decision: Phase 22 chosen over closing 20/21's PARTIAL criteria, settling rulings, or running the milestone audit
decisions.rationale: It is the last unexecuted v1.1 phase, it runs last by design because it certifies what every other phase wired, and WIRE-02 is the milestone's last unticked requirement.

decisions.decision: Execute Phase 22 INLINE and sequentially, not via spawned executor agents
decisions.rationale: execute-phase.md sanctions this: 'Other runtimes: use sequential inline execution as the fallback.' Also avoids the workflow's gsd-sdk state writers, which CLAUDE.md bans after three separate corruptions of STATE.md.

decisions.decision: The elfconv loader port and the function-sizing fix are TWO commits, never one
decisions.rationale: The port's entire warrant is 'nothing changed' - byte-identical bitcode and wasm on both loader paths. The sizing fix deliberately changes output. Both claims cannot hold in one patch.

decisions.decision: Upstream PRs exclude our build-system changes
decisions.rationale: Trimming llvm_map_components_to_libnames and gating tests behind REMILL_ENABLE_TESTING serve a downstream WebAssembly build, not upstream. Offered in the PR body rather than pushed.

context_notes: The approach that paid off all session: treat every document's claim about the code as a hypothesis and measure it. Six claims turned out false this session - elfconv's README on x86, the praxis review on verifyChain, two of my own comments written before verification, a commit message asserting Phase 26 items were deleted when they are live, and 22-01's own corpus counts. The single most valuable habit is the watched-red plant: it caught a green build with a correct function count and wrong bitcode, which no count-based check would have seen. Phase 22 is ABOUT that failure mode - three cheap tracers scored the same corpus 54, 3 and 102 - so its Task 3 two-granularity reading is not ceremony, it is the only thing standing between this phase and a tautology.
